terms.gloss: stop off at, turn aside to (a person, an inn) on a journey
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, intransitive, with ad
evidence: Lewis & Short: dēvertere ad caupōnem, ad hospitem (Varr. RR 3.4.9; Cic. Div. 1.57)
terms.comment: Also as a deponent, dēvertor. Latin turns off the road: dē-vertō, turn aside.

terms.gloss: stay with someone as a guest
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.22: cum Athēnīs apud eum dēversārer (Lewis & Short)

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 108.
